name: Green Data Center Università di Pisa - Edificio Server

profile.address: San Piero a Grado, Pisa, Italy
profile.reading: This is the University of Pisas Green Data Center, also referred to by its Edificio Server, or server building, designation, located in the San Piero a Grado area of Pisa, Italy. Following a recent expansion the university describes it as Italys largest university data center, growing from 66 to 104 racks with 38 added, and supporting roughly 700 compute nodes, an estimated 25,000 to 30,000 CPU cores, more than 100 GPU accelerators including Nvidia DGX systems, roughly 200 terabytes of RAM, and all flash storage connected at 25 to 400 gigabits per second. The facility runs at a reported power usage effectiveness of about 1.2, using hot aisle containment, dual independent power feeds with redundant uninterruptible power supplies, and recently added liquid cooling technology from Vertiv, including Liebert XDU units and HyperCool systems paired with latest generation Lenovo Neptune servers the university says cut energy use by up to 40 percent in supported workloads. It is described as the only Italian university data center to hold Classificazione A status from AgID, Italys national digital agency. Network connectivity runs at 200 gigabits per second internally and 100 gigabits per second externally via a second connection node on GARR-T, Italys national research and education network. The facility supports high performance and scientific computing, artificial intelligence research, and university involvement in 5G and quantum computing initiatives, and is shared with the wider regional research community beyond the university itself. The facility originally launched in late 2016 with 250 square meters, or roughly 2,700 square feet, of technical space and 66 racks, built using in-row cooling and separate power supply circuits to achieve its efficient design from the outset, before growing through subsequent expansions to its current 104 rack, largest-in-Italy university data center status.
